out_items.name: In-use utensils properly stored

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Observed utensils being stored in a water container at 66F on the counter next to cook line
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. PIC cleaned and sanitized utensils properly.

out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' EHS observed no illness reporting agreement in place during time of inspection.
violations.corrective_action: A complete employee health policy must have the following elements: 1) Employee training on foodborne illness, particularly symptoms of illness and prevention of the Big Six illnesses (see 'What is Foodborne Illness' handout); and 2) Documentation that employees have been instructed of their responsibility to report symptoms of, diagnosis of or exposure to foodborne illness to management (see 'Employee Illness Reporting Agreement' handout); and 3) A management plan to restrict or exclude employees, as applicable, who have symptoms, diagnosis or exposure to foodborne illness (see 'Employee Illness Decision Guide for PIC/CFM' handout). The information provided at the time of this inspection will help you develop and implement this policy. EHS provided a written copy of Employee Illness reporting agreement to PIC, employees will read, sign, and agree to the policy. Ensure forms are available at the follow up.

out_items.name: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events

violations.title: Clean-up of vomiting and diarrheal events
violations.observation: The food establishment does not have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events. EHS observed no written directions for vomit and diarrhea cleanup
violations.corrective_action: A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. EHS provided a written copy of vomit and diarrhea cleanup instructions to PIC

out_items.name: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use

violations.title: Eating, Drinking, or Using Tobacco
violations.observation: A food employee was observed eating, smoking, or drinking in areas where they may contaminate food, clean equipment, utensils or other items needing protection. EHS observed employee drinking from an open container in the food prep area
violations.corrective_action: Food employees may only eat, drink, or use tobacco in a designated area like a dining room or office area. Employees shall not eat or drink in the kitchen areas, warewashing areas, or storage areas where items may become contaminated. PIC disposed of the open container, instructed employees to not drink from open containers in the food prep area

out_items.name: Hands clean and properly washed

violations.title: Cleaning Procedure
violations.observation: Observed food employees using improper handwashing procedures. EHS OBSERVED EMPLOYEE REMOVE GLOVES, RINSE HANDS AND THEN PROCEED TO CHANGE TASKS.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wash their hands and exposed portions of their arms by: 1) discarding used gloves; 2) rinsing under warm running water; 3) applying soap; 4) rubbing together for at least 10-15 seconds; 5) rinsing thoroughly under warm running water; and 6) drying with paper towels or air drying device. PIC INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEE TO WASH HANDS USING SOAP AND HOT WATER, AND SCRUB FOR AT LEAST 20 SECONDS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION AND PROPER DEMONSTRATION OF HAND WASHING BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP. ZEFFIRELLI RISTORANTE ITALIANO (Inspection Date: 11/12/2024) Page 2 of 7

violations.title: When to Wash
violations.observation: A food employee failed to wash his or her hands before engaging in food preparation, after touching bare human body parts, after coughing, sneezing, eating, after handling soiled utensils, or after engaging in any activity that could contaminate the hands. EHS OBSERVED EMPLOYEES CHANGING TASKS AND NOT WASHING HANDS OR CHANGING GLOVES.
violations.corrective_action: ALL food employees shall wash their hands OFTEN especially after handling trash, using the restroom, handling raw meats, handling soiled equipment and utensils, BEFORE putting on clean gloves, etc. Proper handwashing frequencies will aid in the reduction of foodborne illness. EHS INSTRUCTED EMPLOYEES ON GLOVE USAGE, HAND WASHING PRACTICES TO INCLUDE HOW AND WHEN. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Handwashing Sink, Water Temp
violations.observation: EHS OBSERVED HAND SINK NEXT TO THE COOK LINE NOT BEING ABLE TO REACH A MINIMUM REQUIRED TEMPERATURE OF 100F
violations.corrective_action: A handwashing sink shall be equipped to provide water at a temperature of at least 100F through a mixing valve or combination faucet. EHS SPOKE TO PIC ABOUT ISSUE, WILL FOLLOW UP IN 10 DAYS TO VERIFY HANDSINK CAN REACH MINIMUM 100F.

violations.title: Handwashing Signage
violations.observation: Observed that sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands is not provided or is not clearly visible at all handwashing sinks used by food employees. EHS OBSERVED HAND SINKS IN THE FOOD PREP AREA, LADIES ROOM, MEN’S ROOM AND BAR WITHOUT HANDWASHING SIGNS.
violations.corrective_action: Provide a visible sign or poster at all handwashing sinks used by food employees that reminds food employees to wash their hands. PIC AGREED TO INSTALL HANDWASHING SIGNS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP. ZEFFIRELLI RISTORANTE ITALIANO (Inspection Date: 11/12/2024) Page 5 of 7

out_items.name: Required records available: shellstock tags, parasite destruction

violations.title: Records, Parasite Destruction, Farm-Raised
violations.observation: The following farm-raised fish served raw or partially cooked were observed without a written statement from the supplier stating that the fish were raised and fed according to 3-402.11(B)(3). PIC DID NOT HAVE PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER DURING TIME OF INSPECTION FOR SALMON FILETS.

FAX a copy of this letter to your inspector and keep this statement on site at the food establishment for 90 days beyond the time of service of the fish. PIC AGREED TO PROVIDE PARASITE DESTRUCTION LETTER BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP IN 10 DAYS.

violations.corrective_action: The identity of the source of shellstock (oysters, clams, mussels) that are sold or served shall be maintained by retaining shellstock tags or labels and marking the tag or label with the date when the last shellstock from the container is sold or served. PIC AGREED TO MARK SHELL STOCK TAGS WITH DATE OF LAST SALE. EHS WILL FOLLOW UP IN TEN DAYS TO VERIFY COMPLIANCE

violations.corrective_action: Shellstock that has been removed from the tagged/labeled container must have a system used to identify source. PIC DISPOSED OF CLAMS.

out_items.name: Proper date marking and disposition

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: 1) OBSERVED SEVERAL VARIETIES OF PREPARED FOODS UNDER REFRIGERATION FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS WHICH INCLUDE SAUCES, COOKED PLANT FOODS, COOKED MEATS, ETC.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO PROPERLY LABEL AND DATE MARK PREPARED FOODS SITTING UNDER REFRIGERATION FOR MORE THAN 24 HOURS. SEE FACT SHEET ON DATE MARKING FOR MORE INFORMATION. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Consumer advisory provided for raw and undercooked food

violations.title: Consumer Advisory for Raw/Undercooked Food, Disclosure
violations.observation: The following raw and/or undercooked foods are provided on the menu, menu board, table tent or brochure without proper disclosure: 1) VEAL CHOP IS NOT IDENTIFIED WITH AN ASTERICK (*) TO SHOW IT CAN BE ORDERED UNDERCOOKED.
violations.corrective_action: The Consumer Advisory shall include a disclosure statement that includes a description of the animal-derived foods as raw/undercooked or identification of the animal-derived foods by asterisking (*) them to a footnote that states that the items are served raw or undercooked, or contain raw or undercooked ingredients. EHS MARKED UP THE LUNCH AND DINNER MENUS TO SHOW CORRECTIONS NEEDED. PLEASE PLACE AN ASTERICK (*) NEXT TO THE VEAL CHOP AND REMOVE THE ASTERICKS (*) FROM FOODS LIKE COOKED SHRIMP, COOKED SNAILS, COOKED MUSSELS, AND CAESAR DRESSING BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO MOVE ALL CHEMICALS TO A SEPARATE STORAGE LOCATION. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

violations.title: Common Name, Working Containers

EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO LABEL ALL SPRAY BOTTLES OF CHEMICALS WITH THE COMMON NAME OF THE CHEMICAL BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Approved thawing methods used

violations.title: Proper Thawing Methods for ROP Fish
violations.observation: EHS OBSERVED ROP FISH IN THE WALK IN COOLER BEING THAWED IN PACKAGING WITHOUT BEING OPENED PRIOR TO THAWING.
violations.corrective_action: EHS SPOKE TO PIC ABOUT ISSUE, EMPLOYEES PROCEEDED TO OPEN ROP FISH PACKAGING.

violations.title: Proper thawing methods used for TCS Foods
violations.observation: Observed the following food thawing using an improper method: EHS OBSERVED SQUID THAWING ON COUNTER AND LOBSTER THAWING IN A BUCKET OF WATER ON THE FLOOR IN THE COOK LINE AREA OUTSIDE OF REFRIGERATION AND NOT UNDER RUNNING WATER.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be thawed using one of the following methods: 1) under refrigeration that maintains the food temperature at 41F or less, 2) completely submerged under running water at a water temperature of 70F or below with a sufficient velocity to agitate and float off loose particles of food as long as held for period of time at a temperature of 41F or less, or 3) as part of a cooking process if the food is cooked as specified by Law or thawed in a microwave oven and immediately transferred to a conventional cooking process. PIC MOVED THAWING LOBSTER AND SQUID TO THE WALK IN COOLER.

out_items.name: Thermometers provided and accurate

violations.observation: The food temperature measuring device is not accurate in degrees F. CFM DIAL FOOD THERMOMETER AT 38F IN ICE WATER BATH.
violations.corrective_action: Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to +/- 2 degrees F in the intended range of use. EHS INSTRUCTED CFM TO ACQUIRE THERMOMETER BEFORE FOLLOW UP IN TEN DAYS.

out_items.name: Food properly labeled, original container

violations.corrective_action: Unless a food item can be easily recognized, all foods and ingredients removed from their original containers and stored in working containers shall be labeled using the common name of the food. For example: cooking oils, salt, sugar, flour, spices, herbs, etc. EMPLOYEES MADE LABELS FOR WORKING CONTAINERS. ENSURE CONTINUED CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Insects, rodents, and animals not present

violations.observation: EHS OBSERVED A GAP ALONG THE BASE OF THE REAR KITCHEN DOOR.
violations.corrective_action: Fill or close holes and other gaps along floors, walls, and ceilings to protect against the entry of insects and rodents. EHS OBSERVED MANAGEMENT TO INSTALL PROPER DOOR SWEEP ON BACK DOOR BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.

out_items.name: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage, and display

violations.title: Ice As Coolant Not Used as Food
violations.observation: Ice used as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food is also for beverage ice or used as food. EHS OBSERVED ICE IN BAR AREA BEING USED AS COOLANT AND FOR BEVERAGES.
violations.corrective_action: After use as a medium for cooling the exterior surfaces of food, packaged foods, beverages, or cooling coils/tubes, the ice may not be used as food. PIC AGREED TO USE SEPARATE ICE FOR BEVERAGES, EHS WILL VERIFY COMPLIANCE IN 10 DAYS.

violations.title: Food Storage 6 inches above Floor

Milk crates, soda crates, or bread racks are not suitable for food storage. EHS INSTRUCTED MANAGEMENT TO PROVIDE EITHER MORE SHELVING UNITS OR DUNNAGE RACKS BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP INSPECTION.

violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall wear hair restraints such as hats, visors, hair nets or beard nets to effectively keep their hair from contacting exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens, and unwrapped single-service items. This section does not apply to food employees such as counter staff who ONLY serve beverages and wrapped or packaged foods, hostesses, and wait staff. EMPLOYEES PUT ON HAIR RESTRAINTS WHILE WORKING IN KITCHEN AREA. EHS WILL VERIFY COMPLIANCE IN 10 DAYS

violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. EHS DISCUSSED WITH MANAGEMENT DESIGNATING AN AREA FOR STORAGE OF EMPLOYEE’S PERSONAL BELONGINGS TO INCLUDE COATS, JACKETS, PURSES, CELL PHONES, ETC. ENSURE CORRECTION BEFORE THE FOLLOW UP.
